source.title: SAMPLE COSTS TO ESTABLISH AN ORCHARD
source.publisher: UC Davis Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics / UC Cooperative Extension

priceYear.quote: Sample costs given for labor, materials, equipment and contract services are based on July 2017 figures.

acresFarmed.quote: The hypothetical farm consists of 100 contiguous acres of land.

interestRatePct.quote: An interest rate of 5.00 percent is used to calculate capital recovery.

operatingInterestRatePct.quote: Interest on operating capital is based on cash operating costs and is calculated monthly until harvest at a nominal rate of 4.50 percent per year.

laborMachineRate.quote: Hourly wages for workers are $15.50 for machine operators and $11.00 per hour non-machine labor.

laborNonMachineRate.quote: Hourly wages for workers are $15.50 for machine operators and $11.00 per hour non-machine labor.

yieldStatement.quote: For this analysis, crop yields ranged from 4,500 to 7,500 pounds per acre and crop prices ranged from $0.60 to $1.80 per ton.

costsPerAcre.title: COSTS PER ACRE TO PRODUCE WALNUTS

operations.name: Pruning: Alt. Year (half of cost shown)
operations.quote: Pruning: Alt. Year (half of cost shown) 0.00 0 0 0 0 130 130

capitalRecoveryFormula.quote: The formula for the calculation of the annual capital recovery costs is ((Purchase Price – Salvage Value) x Capital Recovery Factor) + (Salvage Value x Interest Rate).

salvageMethod.quote: Salvage value is an estimate of the remaining value of an investment at the end of its useful life.

propertyTaxRatePct.quote: For this study, county taxes are calculated as 1 percent of the average value of the property.

machineLaborFactor.quote: Labor for operations involving machinery are 20 percent higher than the operation time given in Table 2 to account for the extra labor involved in equipment set up, moving, maintenance, work breaks, and field repair.
